title: Braves add OF Lane Thomas, LHP Bailey Falter in trade with Royals
content:
As they bid to run away with the National League East, the Atlanta Braves on Saturday evening acquired outfielder Lane Thomas and left-handed pitcher Bailey Falter from the Kansas City Royals for two minor-league pitchers, righty Lucas Braun and lefty Carter Holton.

Thomas exited the Royals’ game against the Rockies in Colorado in the fourth inning and received hugs from teammates in the visitors dugout. It’s the fourth time in his career that he’s been traded, and the third time it’s happened in the days leading up to the deadline.

Thomas owns a .232/.326/.393 slash line this season, but has a track record of faring well against left-handed pitching. He boasts an .800 OPS against lefties this year. The Braves have a .706 OPS as a team against lefties, which ranks in the middle of the pack in MLB, versus a .745 mark against righties.

Thomas signed a one-year, $5.25 million deal with the Royals over the winter, opting for new surroundings rather than a return to the Cleveland Guardians on a similar contract. The Guardians acquired him ahead of the 2024 trade deadline, and he delivered a go-ahead grand slam off Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal in the decisive game of the ALDS that October. Thomas spent last year dealing with foot and wrist injuries.

Falter was set to join the Royals’ rotation after a stint in Triple-A Omaha following a couple of rough stretches in Kansas City earlier this season. He has allowed 15 runs on 24 hits in 9 2/3 innings in the big leagues this year. The 29-year-old lefty logged a 3.35 ERA with Omaha, and likely will head to Triple A for the Braves.

Braun, a 6-foot, 185-pound righty, attacks hitters with six pitches, led by a sweeping slider. Although lacking a plus offering, he thrives on his command, advanced control and an ability to mix speeds effectively. He had a 3.92 ERA in 10 games with Triple-A Gwinnett.

Holton, the Braves’ second-round pick in 2024, missed all of 2025 as he recovered from Tommy John surgery. He had a 5.08 ERA in six games with High-A Augusta this season.
